sections.hypothesis: A pair whose price has risen over the last 12 months tends to keep rising, and one that fell tends to keep falling, enough that holding each pair long or short in the direction of its 12-month trend, sized to equal volatility, earns a positive Sharpe after spreads and overnight financing, 2006-2022, before the forex holdout.
sections.rationale:
Who pays: participants who trade currencies for reasons other than return and adjust slowly: central banks smoothing or defending rates, hedgers rolling fixed programmes, and investors who under-react to news (the behavioural account in the paper). Trend followers are paid for providing liquidity to them and for bearing the risk of sharp reversals.

Outside evidence: Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012, Journal of Financial Economics, 'Time series momentum') find 12-month time-series momentum in all 58 futures and forwards they test, currencies included; Hurst, Ooi and Pedersen ('A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing', 2017) find it across 1880-2016. Against it, stated before running: currency momentum is widely reported to have weakened after 2008, so a small or negative result here would not be surprising.

Not a variant of a rejected family (pullbacks, chart patterns, reversals). DISCLOSED: the trend family is the one Kestrel's crypto research found anything in (trend-vol-target), and trend-vol-target lost money on Binance's EURUSDT and GBPUSDT (2020-01 to 2025-10, Sharpe -0.68 and -0.88, dropped), which saw EUR/USD and GBP/USD including 2023-25. The rule here is the published one at its textbook settings, not tuned from those results. The 10 pairs share currencies (USD in 6, EUR, GBP and JPY in 3 each), so they are fewer independent bets than 10.

The first forex note: the first trial in the forex pool, so the luck bar is 0 and the deflated Sharpe equals P(true Sharpe > 0) for this run. The published evidence is what makes one trial a fair test.
sections.rules:
Implementation fx:trend (kestrel.strategies.fx_trend), all 10 [fx] pairs, daily candles from OANDA with weekend candles dropped (Luke, 2026-11-23). At each day's close (17:00 New York), for each pair on its own candles: the trend is the log change of the mid close over the last 252 trading days; volatility is the standard deviation of the last 60 daily log returns, times sqrt(260). Weight = sign(trend) x 3% / volatility (long if the trend is up, short if down; 0 until both windows are full). If the sum of |weights| would pass 3x ([fx] max_gross_leverage), every weight is scaled down by the same factor. A pair with no candle on a day keeps its weight. Trades fill at the next open through kestrel.backtest.fx_engine: buys at the ask, sells at the bid, the 2% no-trade band, financing each calendar night at the two currencies' OECD 3-month rates less the 1.0% markup (measured from OANDA, 2026-11-23), profit and loss in AUD.

One run: kestrel fx-backtest --research <this note> --warmup-from 2005-01 --start 2006-02 --end 2022-12 --cash 500. The strategy sees candles from 2005-01 (2002-04 is snapshots, not used); the account trades from 2006-02, the first month both windows are full. Nothing from 2023 (the forex holdout) is touched.
sections.parameters: lookback_days 252, vol_days 60, target_vol_pct 3 (each pair's annual volatility target), max_gross_pct 300 (the [fx] cap). From the engine and config: 2% no-trade band, 1.0% financing markup, 500 AUD. Annualising: 260 trading days a year for the volatility input; results on calendar days (365), as every Kestrel result. Nothing is tuned.
sections.costs: Spread from the data on every fill (OANDA's bid and ask at the open; median before the holdout 2.5 pips on EURUSD to 9.6 on GBPJPY). Financing every night on the notional, at the rate difference less the 1.0% markup, both long and short; the report gives carry's share of the profit and the cost of a 2.5% markup. No commission (OANDA's practice pricing is spread-only). One run, one trial in the forex pool; at most three if (6) is reached.
